rejectionReason: The workflow is an informational analytics and reporting process whose sole observable effect is generating a periodic GitHub Discussion summarizing trailing 30-day PR prompt patterns. No discrete repository entity (issue, PR, or file) is assigned for remediation or state transition, discussion creation is activity/output volume rather than operational attainment, and downstream repository merge rates lack discrete per-run opportunity assignment, have total window overlap across daily runs, and cannot be causally attributed or deterministically scored without subjective agent judgment.

decisions.selected: Treat workflow intent as periodic retrospective analytics and informational guidance to assist developers writing Copilot PR prompts.
alternatives: Treat workflow intent as direct automated PR remediation or prompt rewriting
decisions.rationale: Workflow prompt specifies mission to analyze last 30 days of PRs, extract keywords, and publish a daily discussion with recommendations; no automated PR editing or repository mutation occurs.

decisions.selected: No discrete, non-overlapping per-run opportunity can be bound to a single workflow run.
alternatives: Bind opportunity to trailing 30-day PR collection
Bind opportunity to future PRs created after the run
decisions.rationale: Daily scheduled runs evaluate overlapping 30-day trailing windows where individual PRs are analyzed by up to 30 successive runs, preventing discrete per-run opportunity isolation.

decisions.selected: Decline run-to-entity assignment due to ambiguous entity attribution and overlapping observation windows.
alternatives: Assign run to daily calendar date key
Assign run to trailing PR list hash
decisions.rationale: Calendar-based or PR-list assignment records execution events but does not bind to an addressable repository entity undergoing an observable state transition.

decisions.selected: Reject discussion artifact creation and downstream repository merge rates as accepted operational evidence.
alternatives: Accept created GitHub Discussion as evidence of attainment
Accept trailing or downstream PR merge rate as evidence of attainment
decisions.rationale: Discussion creation is safe-output activity rather than repository outcome attainment. Downstream PR merge rates reflect multifactorial engineering outcomes confounded by scope, reviewer availability, and code domain rather than the prompt analysis discussion.

decisions.selected: Indeterminate maturation horizon due to the absence of a bounded downstream state transition.
alternatives: 7-day forward observation window for developer adoption
decisions.rationale: Because no discrete repository opportunity is assigned, no definite cutoff timestamp exists after which evidence stabilizes into a mature operational outcome.

decisions.selected: Block metric formulation because no direct operational attainment metric in [0,1] is defensible without substituting activity, output volume, or unassigned macro proxies.
alternatives: Prompt specificity scoring via LLM grader
decisions.rationale: Discussion creation measures output activity; trailing merge rate measures historical input rather than run effects; prompt scoring relies on subjective agent judgment prohibited by the operational-value contract.

decisions.selected: Omit baseline definition due to blocked design outcome.
alternatives: Historical repository PR merge rate prior to commit 134fc10e16a282117bfb386199c1d775a0a8f288
decisions.rationale: Without a valid primary operational metric, comparable pre-adoption baseline scoring cannot be computed.

uncertainties.description: Changes in developer prompt writing and PR merge success rates cannot be causally attributed to reading the daily prompt analysis discussion versus normal developer learning, tool improvements, or task variation.
Daily scheduled execution causes severe overlap across 30-day trailing PR analysis windows, making independent run-to-opportunity binding impossible.
Evaluating prompt quality, specificity, and adherence to recommendations deterministically from repository artifacts is impossible without subjective natural language evaluation or LLM judging.
Developer consumption, engagement, and actual reading of posted discussions are unobservable in repository git trees or GitHub API metadata.
